autonomy: --auto: approves every permission not explicitly denied
notes: Same MiniMax-M3 on the same key. opencode resolves minimax/MiniMax-M3 from models.dev and reads MINIMAX_API_KEY from the environment; the key is forwarded explicitly because an isolated container inherits nothing from the operator's shell. It has NO endpoint env var — it honours neither MINIMAX_BASE_URL nor ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL — so under --isolate, where the only reachable peer is the recording proxy, it would have no route to the model and lose every trial for a plumbing reason. Its config file DOES take a provider baseURL: verified against 1.18.25 by pointing it at a local server, which received POST /v1/messages — the same Anthropic wire shape claude-code produces, so the proxy and its rate card need no special case. baseURL carries the /v1 suffix because opencode appends /messages to it. The config is rendered per trial (the sidecar proxy's IP is allocated when it joins the network, so this cannot be a committed file) and lands in the evidence bundle beside the number. configSeed pre-populates that dir because opencode npm-installs @opencode-ai/plugin (62 MB) into a fresh XDG_CONFIG_HOME on first run, --pure included, and an isolated container has no network to install it from — measured by pointing it at an empty dir and watching node_modules appear. XDG_CONFIG_HOME pointing at the generated dir is also the FAIRNESS correction it used to be on its own: without it opencode loads ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json and every MCP server in it, which on this machine gave it nine tools freecode does not have (contextcarry x7, figma x2). Measured, not assumed — asking it to list its tools returned 19 with the operator's config and 10 without. Neither --pure nor OPENCODE_CONFIG suppresses MCP; only XDG_CONFIG_HOME does. --pure additionally drops external plugins.
